evals.prompt: Use TDD to implement a FizzBuzz function in Python. It should return 'Fizz' for multiples of 3, 'Buzz' for multiples of 5, 'FizzBuzz' for multiples of both, and the number as a string otherwise.
evals.expected_output: A fizzbuzz.py file with the implementation and a test_fizzbuzz.py file. Tests are written before the corresponding implementation. The implementation grows in small steps driven by successive tests.
expectations: A test file exists and contains at least 4 tests covering plain number, multiple of 3, multiple of 5, and multiple of 15
The production code file exists and all tests pass
The agent described or produced a test list before writing any code
The first test written is for a plain number (not the full FizzBuzz case), showing simplest-first ordering
No production code exists that is not covered by at least one test

evals.prompt: Use TDD to implement a Stack class in Python with push, pop, peek, and is_empty methods. pop on an empty stack should raise an IndexError.
evals.expected_output: A stack.py file with the Stack implementation and a test_stack.py file. Tests drive each method in turn, starting from is_empty.
expectations: A test for is_empty on a new stack appears before any Stack implementation
Tests cover all four methods: push, pop, peek, is_empty
A test verifies that pop on an empty stack raises IndexError
All tests pass with the final implementation
Tests were added one at a time — no large batches of tests written before the code caught up

evals.prompt: There is a bug: a discount function applies a 10% discount twice when both vip=True and code='SAVE10' are supplied. Use TDD to write a reproducing test first, then fix it.
evals.expected_output: A failing test that reproduces the bug, followed by the minimal fix. The test was written before the fix was applied.
expectations: A test for the combined vip=True and code='SAVE10' case is written and confirmed to fail before any fix is applied
The fix is minimal — only the double-discount logic is changed
All tests pass after the fix
No unrelated behaviour was changed alongside the fix

evals.prompt: Use TDD to implement a function that returns the sum of a list of integers. Start from the simplest case.
evals.expected_output: An implementation that evolves through multiple transformation steps: constant return for empty list, then variable for single-element list, then iteration for multi-element list.
expectations: The first test is for an empty list returning 0
The implementation for the empty-list test returns the constant 0, not a general loop
A second test for a single-element list forces a more general approach
Iteration or equivalent is only introduced once a two-or-more-element test forces it
All tests pass with the final implementation

evals.prompt: Use TDD to implement a function that checks whether a string is a palindrome (reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring case and non-alphanumeric characters).
evals.expected_output: A palindrome.py and test_palindrome.py. Tests start simple (empty string or single character) and build up to the full normalisation logic.
expectations: A test list or plan is described before implementation starts
Tests cover: empty string, single character, simple palindrome, simple non-palindrome, mixed-case palindrome, palindrome with spaces or punctuation
All tests pass with the final implementation
The refactor phase removes any duplication introduced while making tests pass
The agent runs the test suite after each Red and Green phase
